claims.text: The proposed baseline is a W–Ta–Ti–V–Cr refractory high-entropy alloy produced by elemental powder mixing and spark plasma sintering.
Elemental powder mixing followed by spark plasma sintering can produce a W-based high-entropy alloy containing in-situ TiC.
Adjusting Ti content and sintering parameters will induce controlled TiC precipitation in W–Ta–Ti–V–Cr.
The intervention will create uniformly dispersed TiC nanoparticles both inside grains and along grain boundaries.
Spark plasma sintering at approximately 1600°C will promote the desired TiC formation.
Helium irradiation near 1023 K and at the proposed fluence represents conditions relevant to plasma-facing components.
TiC nanoparticles will act as pinning centers that inhibit irradiation-induced defect migration.
TiC nanoparticles will inhibit grain-boundary mobility during helium irradiation.
Inhibiting defect migration and grain-boundary mobility will mitigate helium-bubble growth and coalescence.
Mitigating helium-bubble growth and coalescence will reduce irradiation-induced embrittlement.
The TiC-containing microstructure will maintain or enhance hardness and strength.
The TiC-engineered alloy will have smaller or less dense helium bubbles than the unmodified alloy.
The TiC-engineered alloy will exhibit a lower irradiation-induced hardening fraction than the unmodified alloy.
The TiC-engineered alloy will retain mechanical properties comparable to or better than those of the unmodified alloy.
Elemental powder mixing and spark plasma sintering provide a practical manufacturing route for refractory high-entropy alloys.
The radiation-tolerance benefit will hold when the microstructure contains a moderate volume fraction of fine TiC precipitates.
Excessive TiC content or a nonuniform TiC distribution may adversely affect ductility.
The cited W-based alloys have enhanced room-temperature hardness and strength.
The optimal TiC volume fraction and spatial distribution for balancing irradiation tolerance and mechanical performance are not established.
